Cc: finance@greenleaf.io

Subject: Private offer question: reseller coupons + invoice routing

Hi Mateo,

Thanks again for walking us through the private offer earlier. A couple of procurement questions came up on our side before we sign the PO:

1) Reseller coupons: Greenleaf sometimes issues reseller coupons to end customers that need to be applied as discounts on the invoice (negative line items). For the Azure private offer, can we (a) include an explicit negative line item on the invoice you send, or (b) receive a separate credit note from Redwood? Which approach is recommended so our accounting system accepts it cleanly?

2) Invoice routing: We need invoices sent to finance@greenleaf.io and the invoice needs an explicit reference to our PO ID (PO-2027-GF-1193). Can you confirm Redwood can ship PDF invoices to that address and populate the PO field?

3) Channel margin visibility: our reseller partner asks to see a simple netback line showing partner commission (not public-facing). Is Redwood able to provide an internal-only invoice variant or an attached reconciliation CSV that shows reseller margin without exposing list prices in the public invoice?

I've attached our draft PO and an example of the invoice layout our AP team prefers. Happy to hop on a quick call if it's faster.

Best,
Tina
Director, Procurement
Greenleaf Analytics

Attachments: Greenleaf_PO_Draft.pdf (pdf, 88KB); Invoice_Routing_Template.xlsx (xlsx, 24KB)

From: mateo_alvarez@redwood.ai
To: Tina Morris <tina@greenleaf.io>
Cc: ben_carter@redwood.ai, irene_choi@redwood.ai
Date: Mon, 10 May 2027 12:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Private offer question: reseller coupons + invoice routing

Hi Tina — thanks, this is helpful. Short answers up front, then implementation details below.

- Reseller coupons: we can support both (a) a negative line item on the invoice, or (b) a separate credit memo. For Azure private offers the usual path is a negative line item because it preserves the PO/Invoice pairing and is easier for automated AP systems. If your tax/legal team prefers a separate credit memo, we can do that too.

- Invoice routing: yes, we can send the final invoice PDF to finance@greenleaf.io and include PO-2027-GF-1193 in the PO reference field.

- Channel margin visibility: we cannot show a partner-only netback on the customer-facing invoice, but we can attach an internal reconciliation CSV (partner_netback_Greenleaf_PO-1193.csv) with the commission line and any pass-throughs. That CSV will be restricted to the billing contact and the partner contact.

Implementation notes:
- If you want the negative line item approach, please confirm the desired invoice line label (e.g., "Reseller coupon - partner code XYZ") and whether the coupon should reduce taxable base (we'll need confirmation from your tax team).
- For credit memos we will: issue a credit referencing the original invoice number and your PO, and that will show up as a separate document.
- I'll coordinate with billing ops to add finance@greenleaf.io as the recipient and to include the PO field. It may take 1-2 business days to change the invoice template for this deal.

Next steps proposed: you confirm preferred coupon handling (invoice negative line vs credit memo) and whether the partner-visible reconciliation CSV is acceptable. Once confirmed we'll run a mock invoice and send it to your finance inbox for validation.

Thanks — Mateo
Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference

Mateo / Irene — quick notes from channel ops perspective before we commit to the negative line approach:

- Azure private offers are signed through Microsoft but Redwood still issues the commercial invoice to the end customer. That invoice must match the amount charged by Microsoft for marketplace passthroughs. If we apply a negative line item on our invoice, we need to ensure the marketplace settlements still reconcile with Microsoft billing. Ops will need to: map the coupon line to an internal credit and then net that down when reconciling the payout to the partner.

- For partner accounting, providing the reconciliation CSV is the path we use for most deals. The CSV contains: SKU, usage_period, list_price, coupon_amount, partner_commission, netback_to_partner. This keeps the customer invoice clean while giving partners the visibility they need.

- One wrinkle: if Greenleaf wants the coupon to reduce the taxable base, we need a formal letter from their tax team indicating acceptance; otherwise we treat coupons as reductions to the invoice total but taxable base remains as originally billed (depending on jurisdiction).

I can draft the CSV template and a short memo for AP and partner ops. Mateo, can you confirm Greenleaf's preference so I can begin mapping?

Ben
Channel Ops
Redwood Inference

From: irene_choi@redwood.ai
To: Tina Morris <tina@greenleaf.io>, mateo_alvarez@redwood.ai
Cc: ben_carter@redwood.ai
Date: Tue, 11 May 2027 11:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Private offer question: reseller coupons + invoice routing

Hi Tina,

From a legal/tax compliance viewpoint, two recommendations:

1) Negative line item is fine, but please specify the legal entity that will be listed as the invoice recipient and the tax ID to appear on the invoice. That must match your AP records to avoid payment delays.

2) If the coupon modifies taxable base, we need written confirmation from your tax advisor stating that the coupon is deductible from VAT/sales tax in your jurisdiction. If none, we will list coupon as a discount but preserve the taxable amounts as required.

3) For the partner reconciliation CSV: include a confidentiality footer and mark the file as "Internal - Partner View Only". We'll include partner_netback_Greenleaf_PO-1193.csv as the reconciliation attachment.

Irene Choi
Senior Counsel, Redwood Inference
